texts: Amicar (aminocaproic acid) decreases the incidence of intracranial haemorrhage: D, as the book gives it.
Aminocaproic acid is an antifibrinolytic: it stops clots from being broken down, and in neonates on ECMO it was reported to reduce bleeding, including intracranial haemorrhage.
Heparin, acting through antithrombin, keeps the circuit from clotting, and the activated clotting time is usually kept around 180 to 220 seconds, lower than 250 to 300.
The protease inhibitor nafamostat does reduce heparin requirements.
In the picture, the little red car guards the dams and the head lantern stays dry.
Memory hook: the AMI car guards the dams, and the head stays dry.
